hypothesis: Replacing the common four TEMP relation-view membership predicate by a correlated reference-ID EXISTS preserves finite declared SQLite rows, types, multiplicity, consumer ordering/pagination, and requested errors, while eliminating the membership subquery's global reference scan in the declared point-query plans.

target.optimized_predicate: EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM temp.reference r WHERE r.id=original.reference_id)
target.unchanged: The reference visibility VIEW, hidden-endpoint NOT IN predicates, catalog JSON DISTINCT, ORDER BY, cursor, LIMIT, and downstream authorization/witness checks are not modified.

novelty: Follow-up to failed ADR1080. The product predicate and result/error/plan contracts are unchanged. Only 18 illegal non-NULL reference_end fixture collisions are repaired. All 1,582 conditions are executed, but the 1,345 already-successful SQL pairs are observed supporting evidence; only the 237 previously unexecuted product-query conditions form the prospective primary subset.
schema_boundary: Published SQLite TEXT-affinity IDs and default BINARY collation, including SQLite-permitted NULL/orphan values and nullable composite-key duplicates. Custom collations, changed affinities and arbitrary schema substitution are outside this equivalence claim. Legacy reference table and production compact payload/body VIEW are both included.
fixture_rules: Every nonempty fixture has visible R00 and hidden-owner R20 controls plus the subject state; empty_reference_set removes all reference rows but retains orphan relation rows.
Mask bits 0..3 assign hidden source endpoints independently to end/target/candidate/candidate_end. Only the first three participate in the existing reference visibility exclusion policy.

The existing NOT IN NULL three-valued behavior is preserved: a NULL reference ID attached to a hidden endpoint may suppress unrelated references. The candidate must not repair that behavior within this change.

Multiplicity uses legal distinct source/ordinal/candidate keys for repeated reference associations; NULL source IDs additionally permit identical reference_end rows under SQLite's nullable composite primary key.
Missing/NULL source links remain governed by existing reference visibility, not newly granted source-reading authority. The separate source projection is checked too.
Navigation latest-only selection activates TEMP views even with no excluded document. The early-return control starts with the normal caller's read-only guard and must install no TEMP relation views.

All normal payload JSON is valid; compact reference schema comes from the frozen arm's unchanged production shared_reference_schema. All original database bytes are immutable after fixture construction.

Only in source_boundary/reference_end, a non-NULL special source occupies index 0; indices 1 and 2 retain their original s-visible-1/2 values. Other roles and nullable source-ID duplicate rows remain unchanged. Exactly the 18 declared case IDs change fixture rows.

consumer_queries.full_projection: Full typed projections of source, reference and all four relation views, ordered by every projected column.
consumer_queries.relation_page: All 4 views x 4 source filters x 3 cursors x 3 limits, preserving reference_id and remaining-column ordering.
consumer_queries.catalog: Existing SELECT DISTINCT r.json JOIN reference_end source/cursor/order/limit form, with the optional json_each only_references restriction; all 4 x 3 x 3 x 3 combinations.
consumer_queries.candidate: Existing reference_candidate reference-ID consumer ordered by ordinal,candidate_id.

oracle: Normal projections and consumers use an independent fixture-row oracle with SQL NULL/IN/NOT IN/BINARY ordering semantics. Both arms must match the oracle and each other exactly, including duplicate rows, tuple value types, column metadata and failures. Missing-relation/requested-malformed errors use exact exception type/message equivalence; each deliberately requested error must actually occur.
plan_gate: For each active-mode/view/layout point query, record full EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN. Baseline must exhibit a reference membership LIST SUBQUERY with a reference-table/payload full scan; optimized must use a CORRELATED subquery and the existing reference-ID index point lookup, with no full reference-table/payload scan for that membership. Hidden endpoint scans remain allowed and separately named. No opcode-count or end-to-end latency claim is made.
immutability: Compare serialized main database SHA256 before/after binding, observations and denied writes. Both arms must preserve PRAGMA query_only=1 and the authorizer's rejection of main DELETE and query_only=OFF; no existing artifact is overwritten.
failure_policy: Stream and flush every paired fixture with raw typed observations to sql-pairs.jsonl.gz. Preserve the first failure in sql-first-failure.json and retain partial census. Stop without changing candidate, expected outputs or completed records.
limits: This finite SQL census does not certify legal meaning or every downstream witness/authorization error. Unchanged downstream code binding and native original-frame checks supply separate evidence.

A malformed JSON payload outside the requested rows may be encountered only by the old global scan. Such global unrequested-corruption exception timing is explicitly outside equivalence; ingestion and generation validation retain that responsibility.
Requested malformed JSON is tested at the selected reference itself. NULL/orphan behavior is preserved rather than silently normalized.
SQLite query-plan categories are mechanism evidence, not measured service acceleration or GENOS Oracle behavior.
No product source, source corpus, model, active MAIN pointer or real-data database is changed by this runner.

evidence_partition.prior_fixture_failure_note: This case previously failed fixture INSERT before Selection.bind or any product consumer SQL. It is included among product-query-unexecuted primary conditions, not described as an unobserved fixture-construction outcome.
